steps.what: Check articles, load condition and permitted extractor or drier settings
Operate extractors and driers or direct operators and respond to abnormal conditions

tasks.design: Keep equipment operation and supervision with the laundry worker using the existing {OTHER} extractor and drier controls. Existing programmed cycles remain equipment runtime and earn no new labour saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Load suitability and abnormal equipment conditions require physical observation and practical response.
tasks.enabler_now: No software-only change establishes a reduction in this operating task.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed fabrics, residual moisture and unusual heat or movement need attention at the machine.
tasks.human_edge: The worker recognizes an unsuitable load and stops or escalates unsafe operation.
tasks.altitude: Operating responsibility and required attendance remain unchanged.

reach.task: Investigate abnormal extractor or drier operation
reach.learn: Clear fault descriptions and the boundary between operation and repair

evidence.claim: Existing automatic cycles do not establish a new saving in operator checks or physical supervision; this task assessment is E1.

assumptions: Boundary covers operating settings, operation and direct supervision, not loading, unloading or separate production records.

The worker produces the load assessment and selected settings in s1 by reading care instructions and observing the articles. All observation time stays counted; no structured fabric or moisture feed is assumed.
The existing controller's native cycles are already used where appropriate. Neither their elapsed runtime nor hypothetical new sensors or robotics are credited as human labour removed.
No changed software, controls or work process is proposed, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Load variability and current programmed cycles
research_questions: Does a real observation study identify any repeated clerical work inside operation rather than existing machine runtime?
